title: Nvidia shares soar more than 30% after Huang reinstated as CEO | CNN Business
html:
Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday and had their third-best day on record after the company announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately.

The announcement turbocharged an already buoyant day for stocks, with the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite surging 6.51%. The S&P 500 soared 4.73%, and the Dow surged 1,448 points, or 3.01%.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 had their best day since April 2025, when stocks soared after President Donald Trump backed down from some tariff threats. The Dow had its best day since November 4, when it rallied sharply after the midterm elections. Tech stocks in Asia, where many suppliers of Nvidia are located, also surged on Tuesday in the wake of Huang’s return.

US stocks had already been poised for a sharp bounce back Monday, following a punishing tech stock sell-off driven by fears about the durability of the AI investment boom. After the news broke shortly before 9:00 a.m. ET that Huang was reinstated, AI stocks skyrocketed, lifting the broader market sharply higher in premarket trading.

Stocks held on to sharp gains throughout trading as investors digested the U-turn. Some of the biggest gainers were technology stocks that have been pummeled recently, with the AI cloud infrastructure company CoreWeave gaining 22.3%.

Nvidia shares rose as much as 36.6% before paring gains slightly and ending the day up 31.48% — their best day since 2003 and a single-day gain of $952 billion in market value.

“The shocking decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO helps to remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, which has been suffering in recent weeks,” Glen Smith, chief investment officer at GDS Wealth Management, wrote in a note.

Relief rally

The rebound comes after a brutal downturn last week, during which all three major US stock indexes recorded weekly losses of 8% or more. The S&P 500 ended the week with its seventh straight day of losses — its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The Nasdaq plunged more than 5% on Friday alone and was sitting in the red for the year before bouncing back on Monday.

“Nvidia is a key player in the whole AI space … particularly with these neoclouds,” said Lance Roberts, chief investment strategist at RIA Advisors. “It’s not surprising you’re seeing this broad relief rally across the whole segment because [Huang’s] return removes a lot of the uncertainty.”

Stocks were already rising premarket before Huang was reinstated. That rebound looked to be in large part “mechanical,” said Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at consultancy Capital Economics.

“It was just such a big sell-off (last week) and got a bit overdone,” he told CNN early Monday, calling the early rebound a “dead cat bounce” — trader speak for a brief recovery in stocks before a downward trend resumes.

After the news of Huang’s return to Nvidia, Goltermann said, “I guess this particular cat has another of its nine lives to live.”

“Short term, the Nvidia news may well extend the rebound further, and clearly helps the bits of the AI supply chain most dependent on Nvidia directly,” Goltermann said, referring to the neoclouds that depend on Nvidia’s financing and chipmakers who develop parts for Nvidia.

“Still think the main challenges for the stock market remain: late cycle red flags across the board, hawkish Fed, tighter funding environment, extremely optimistic earnings forecasts to hit,” Goltermann added. “So we still expect that the general direction of travel over the next few months will be down.”

As of Monday’s market close, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are down 7.4% and 12.7%, respectively, from their peaks on October 6. The Dow is down 8.75% since its peak on August 5.

Markets have been roiled by growing investor doubt about how sustainable the AI boom is. Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO last week did little to quell investor concerns about potential regulation, sky-high company valuations and a slowdown in AI investment, particularly for data centers.

“What began in October as a textbook rotation out of tech from extended levels has morphed into a broader risk-off move amid a succession of negative catalysts,” Deutsche Bank analysts wrote in a note Monday before the announcement from Nvidia.

They cited the Democratic “blue wave” in the US midterms; the troubles at Nvidia, a company crucial to the AI rollout; the wave of equity hitting stock markets as firms tied to AI go public; “and a cluster of seemingly concurrent tech outages that have raised wider concerns.”

Asian stocks surged Tuesday local time. Taiwan’s benchmark Taiex index, anchored by the world’s largest contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), jumped 9% during Tuesday’s trading day.

South Korea’s Kospi, dominated by memory giants SK Hynix and Samsung, closed up 6.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 3.9% over the day.

Nvidia accounted for about one-fifth of TSMC’s revenue and nearly one-fourth of SK Hynix’s last year. The fallout from the Huang scandal has triggered historic declines and wiped out quarters of gains in the tech powerhouses of Taiwan, South Korea and Japan. The rout has prompted financial regulators in Taiwan, South Korea and China to announce measures to support markets.

In Europe, markets were positive. Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker ASML was up nearly 9%.

“Love him or hate him, Jensen brings a lot of credibility and financing,” Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, told CNN.

“That ball was under the water by a lot. Now we have a pop. When you’re this oversold, usually that bounce can continue,” Detrick said.

The worst is likely over for this market scare for now, he said, although the market is “not out of the woods,” especially as Huang still has to testify on Capitol Hill in December.

CNN’s Matt Egan and John Liu contributed reporting.
summary: Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday and had their third-best day on record after the company announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately.
